title: Use the larger model where reasoning earns its cost
lead: The proposed hybrid system lets a larger model plan a subgoal or help label training examples. A small local policy handles supported decisions and abstains when it lacks enough evidence.

title: Make the fallback and its cost explicit
lead: Hybrid mode can route uncertainty to a configured provider; local-only mode cannot silently make that request. The intended GLM identity and interface must be pinned. Network travel, reasoning, and recovery remain part of task latency.

title: A constrained API is not proof of shared-cache branching
lead: A hosted endpoint may accept a schema while withholding the state, logits, masks, and batching controls needed for faithful RLCD. Actual runtime capabilities decide whether the larger-model experiment is feasible.

title: Two experiments with different tradeoffs
lead: Reducing output work in a powerful model and teaching a small policy are separate approaches. Neither eliminates neural computation nor guarantees preservation of general capabilities. A documented feasibility no-go still leaves useful baseline and student experiments.

title: Count the entire path to a completed task
lead: Observation, inference, transport, execution, fallback, and recovery all contribute to what the user waits for. Controlled candidate comparisons need a broader generated-action baseline to expose missing coverage.

title: Recorded history cannot answer an unobserved counterfactual
lead: Closed-loop quality needs live resettable environments. Freeze gates before selection, choose on development data, calibrate separately, and reserve the final test for evaluation. These visuals illustrate the protocol and report no measured speedup.
